transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-09-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (CTO, Marigold); Priya Desai (ML Eng, Marigold); Leo Park (Product)
Agenda: intro, current infra+constraints, model selection (open models + context), tool-calling/plug-ins, deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), security requirements, next steps

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Marigold needs a multimodel setup for chat and retrieval with 32k+ context, heavy multilingual support (EN/ES/ZH), and tool-calling for database lookups and ticket creation. They are leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to PII and audit needs but want a hosted pilot if possible for speed to value. Security controls required: SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2 evidence.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Alex Rivera, I'll drive commercial on this side. Maya is our solutions engineer, she'll cover technical fit. Jordan, Priya, Leo, thanks for making time.
00:12 Jordan (Marigold): Yeah thanks, um, appreciate it. We, we wanted to walk through options — model choice especially — we have mixed language support and long chat threads so context size matters.
00:25 Maya (Redwood SE): Great, sounds good. Can you give us a bit of background on current stack and traffic patterns?
00:33 Priya: Sure. Currently we run a microservices infra on AWS, ECS for API, Postgres for user data. The chat product stores conversations; average session length is about 6 turns but we have occasional long threads that need 20k-40k tokens. Throughput is modest, peak 30 qps for chat generation. We also do retrieval from our vector DB for knowledge-rich responses.
00:55 Leo: And compliance is important — we have regulated customer data in EMEA. Audits are on the roadmap so data residency and audit logs required.
01:07 Maya: Got it. For model selection, do you have a preferred open model family today? Any internal evals?
01:15 Priya: We've run some small evals on Llama2- and Mistral-derived checkpoints and a couple of community quantized variants. The quality is ok but we see hallucinations in tool-calling scenarios and switching languages isn't always great.
01:35 Alex: Okay, that matches what we typically see. From our side we usually recommend a mix: a strong 32k-context model for the long-thread cases and a faster quantized 8k variant for short interactions to save cost. We can orchestrate routing between them — weighted by latency or cost.
01:55 Jordan: When you say orchestrate, are you talking about Redwood routing? Would that be on Hosted?
02:02 Maya: Yes, our smart routing can run on Hosted, Dedicated, or Private — it's an API-level policy. For example, route requests with >8k prefix length to a 32k model hosted on Dedicated, fall back to 8k if capacity is constrained. The same policy files work across deployment modes.
02:25 Jordan: Hmm, our security team will want VPC and KMS. Likely we need Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment. But we'd prefer a Hosted pilot if that speeds things up.
02:38 Alex: Totally reasonable. We commonly do a Hosted pilot for 2-4 weeks, then migrate to Dedicated or Private for production. Hosted pilot doesn't expose your production data if you send anonymized samples. For PII, Private is the safest.
02:52 Priya: Can you support tool-calling? We need DB lookups and ticket creation via a secure webhook. Also we need structured output (JSON) from the model.
03:03 Maya: Yes — we support function/tool calling and structured output. Caveat: some open models are better at deterministic JSON output. We have eval stats across models in the catalog we can share. Also, for tool safety we recommend RL randomization? no, sorry, meaning we pair JSON schema validation with a light model-level parser to reduce hallucinated calls.
03:28 Priya: (laughs) parser, yeah that's what we need — a deterministic layer.
03:33 Jordan: What about multilingual performance — Spanish & Mandarin are mandatory. Do you recommend a single multilingual model or per-language specialist?
03:41 Maya: For robustness, we usually pick a model family with proven multilingual pretraining for EN/ES/ZH. Some customers route Spanish to a finetuned Spanish-specialist for cost/quality. There's a tradeoff.
03:56 Alex: To add, latency vs cost: a 32k float16 model on a larger GPU has higher cost but keeps latency acceptable. Quantized int8/4 variants cut cost but sometimes increase latency per token slightly depending on runtime kernels.
04:16 Priya: How about KV cache across sessions? We want to cache prefixes for re-runs and reranking.
04:24 Maya: We support KV cache reuse with sticky routing; prefix caching reduces re-computation. For retrieval-heavy flows, we recommend embedding caches and partial caching of intermediate vectors.
04:38 Jordan: Any benchmarks you can share for a 32k context on NVidia H100s or equivalent? We need ballpark latency at 8-12 tokens/sec output and cost per 1k tokens.
04:52 Alex: I'll attach our benchmark sheet. Quick numbers: on H100-class instance with optimized kernels, 32k decode at 20-30 t/s for common models; cost depends on quantization and batching. We'll send weighted examples tailored to your payload.
05:09 Maya: Also note Dedicated has predictable throughput SLAs; Private can be tuned for your infra but you shoulder ops.

05:35 Jordan: Security checklist — SSO (SAML/Okta), SOC2 docs, KMS integration, audit logs, data retention controls, and support for in-region hosting (EU). Can Redwood satisfy those?
05:49 Alex: Yes — SSO via SAML, KMS/HSM integrations for Private, audit logs available in the Console. We have SOC2 type II report; I'll link it. For EU residency, Dedicated or Private with region pinning is preferred.
06:03 Priya: Great. About model updates and rollouts — we need canary testing and fallback if a new model regresses.
06:13 Maya: Our rollout supports canary and A/B with automatic fallback based on quality/regression alerts. We integrate eval sets and prompt tests so you can gate rollouts.
06:27 Leo: Can we run a POC with our real traffic behind a feature flag? We'll need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
06:36 Alex: Yes, Redwood Console shows per-route latency/cost, token breakdown, and trace hooks. We'll set up a dashboard in the pilot.

07:00 (rapid cross-talk: brief clarifications on token accounting and data retention)

07:45 Priya: About tool-calling security — the webhook needs to only accept signed requests from Redwood and support per-call RBAC.
07:55 Maya: We support signed webhooks and HMAC; you can also route through your proxy for extra checks. For RBAC we integrate with your identity provider for API keys.
08:10 Jordan: Are there any gotchas with open-model hallucinations when doing tool-calling, or does Redwood add guardrails?
08:20 Maya: We add multiple layers: schema validation, a confirmation step in the dialog for destructive actions, and reranking of tool-call proposals using a smaller verifier model.
08:35 Priya: Ok. For multilingual tool-calling we'll need the verifier to work across languages.
08:41 Maya: We can finetune or use a multilingual verifier; we have experience with that.

09:00 Jordan: Let's talk about data flows — what logs are persisted and where? We need to prove no PII is stored in Hosted pilot.
09:11 Alex: Default retention is 30 days for Hosted; Dedicated/Private you control retention. We can do redaction or on-the-fly masking. For the pilot we recommend anonymizing traffic on your side and share a redaction recipe.
09:30 Priya: We'll provide anonymized corpus for initial bench.

10:02 (longer discussion on routing policy examples; Maya walks through pseudo policy)

15:20 Maya: Example policy: if language detected = zh or context > 8k -> route to model ×32k; else route to ×8k-quant. Fallback: if latency > threshold -> degrade to cheaper variant. We can do weighted splits for A/B.

18:12 Jordan: For cost projection — can you model expected monthly costs at 30 qps peak and average 6-turn sessions with 1k avg tokens per session?
18:24 Alex: We'll run a cost model — need your token distribution; Priya will share. We'll return a 6-12 month cost projection with Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private scenarios.

22:00 Priya: Any limits on streaming and function arguments size? We need to stream long responses and pass structured payloads of ~10-20KB.
22:12 Maya: Streaming is supported; function payloads up to X KB (we'll confirm exact limit in follow-up; I'd say we typically handle 64KB serialized but that's model-dependent). We'll confirm.

25:40 Leo: Competitor question — we sometimes evaluate Anthropic and OpenAI for few-shot quality and tool-calling. How is Redwood different?
25:52 Alex: Redwood focuses on serving and ops — we don't just expose models; we provide the runtime, routing, caching, and observability for production inference across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We also provide model catalog + suggestions for quantization and batching — operational levers that affect unit economics.
26:13 Jordan: Cool. Any constraints for on-prem? We have air-gapped clusters for certain customer data.
26:22 Maya: Private on-prem supports air-gapped deployments; you'll run a control plane connector or self-managed control plane depending on version. We'll need some planning for kernel compatibility and hardware.

30:00 (silence while Maya shares a screen — audio notes omitted)

33:10 Priya: We also wondered about embeddings quality and vector DB recommendations — we run Pinecone for now but might switch.
33:21 Maya: Embedding quality depends on model. For retrieval we recommend a high-quality embedding model and vector DB with hybrid search. We have connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, etc.

37:05 Jordan: Timeline — ideally pilot in next 2 weeks, production in 8–12 weeks after pilot if all good. Any blockers?
37:15 Alex: Sounds feasible. Blocks: signed NDA/contract, access to sample data, and confirmation of pilot deployment mode.
37:28 Priya: We'll aim to send samples by EOD next Wednesday.

40:00 (action item recap)
40:12 Alex: Quick recap — Redwood will: 1) share SOC2+security pack link, 2) send pilot pricing and SOW, 3) run perf back-of-envelope for 32k context, 4) set up a console demo. Marigold will: share anonymized corpus, confirm SSO provider, confirm desired pilot model variants.
40:36 Jordan: That matches our notes.

41:00 (questions)
41:12 Leo: How do you handle cold starts and kernel warm-up?
41:20 Maya: We use pre-warmed pools and continuous batching; cold starts are minimized with warm workers. For Dedicated we guarantee warmed capacity options.
41:38 Jordan: Is there a minimum commit for Dedicated?
41:44 Alex: Yes, Dedicated is typically a reserved capacity contract — we can propose monthly vs annual tiers in the pricing sheet.

45:00 Priya: Anything else on eval criteria? We need to measure hallucination rate on tool-calls and multilang BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics.
45:12 Maya: We'll help set up evaluation harness and suggested test prompts. We can run regression alerts during rollouts.

48:00 (closing)
48:12 Alex: Thanks all, we'll send the links: SOC2, perf spreadsheet, pilot SOW, and a proposal for Hosted pilot first. Link to deck: https://redwood.app/decks/marigold-poc
48:28 Jordan: Great, thanks. We'll look for the docs and aim to have the sample dataset by 2026-09-15.
48:40 Alex: Perfect. Talk soon.
